newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Threatened gas attack on HK subway not carried out.
newsitem.headline: Threatened gas attack on HK subway not carried out.

text.p: A threatened gas attack on Hong Kong's subway train system failed to materialise on Tuesday evening, a police spokesman said.

Last week, the police received a threatening call that a group would launch a gas attack on the local rail netowrk. A government source told Reuters the caller said the attack would be staged on Tuesday night.
By 9:30 p.m. (1330 GMT) on Tuesday, police had received no reports of gas attacks, a police spokesman said by phone.

A local mass circulation Chinese-language daily linked the threat to a dispute over Japanese and Chinese sovereignty claims to a group of East China Sea islands. The dispute has fuelled protests among Chinese communities in Asia in recent months.

The paper said the Aum Shinri Kyo (Supreme Truth) sect, accused of behing behind deadly nerve gas attacks on the Tokyo subway in 1995, had threatened the attack in revenge after Hong Kong and Taiwan activists landed on the islands last week.
The police had declined to comment on the newspaper report.
